title: How Long the Loan Has Been on the Books, and the Rounding of the Charge This Charter Fixes
content:
How the figure that survives the ceiling is rounded, when a late charge on a loan of the Auto Loans line is put right, follows how long the loan has been on the books, counted in whole months from the date it funded to the day of the correction.

1. Where the loan was funded at least 36 whole months before the correction, the figure that survives the ceiling is rounded down to the whole dollar.
2. Where the loan was funded at least 24 but less than 36 whole months before the correction, the figure that survives the ceiling is rounded half-up to the whole dollar.
3. Where the loan was funded less than 24 whole months before the correction, the figure that survives the ceiling is rounded half-up to the cent.

## The three conventions on one figure

Take a figure of 22.50 surviving the ceiling. On a loan funded 40 whole months before the correction it is rounded down to 22.00. On a loan funded 30 whole months before it is rounded half-up to 23.00. On a loan funded 12 whole months before it stands at 22.50.

Take a figure of 15.40 instead. At 40 whole months it becomes 15.00; at 30 whole months it becomes 15.00, since the cents are below the half; at 12 whole months it stands at 15.40.

## Where the bands meet

A loan funded exactly 36 whole months before the correction takes the first convention, the boundary month belonging to it. A loan funded exactly 24 whole months before takes the second, for the same reason. A loan funded 23 whole months before takes the third.
